title: A Sugar Cube That Weighs a Billion Tons

beats.narration: This is an ordinary sugar cube. A piece of a neutron star the same size would weigh a billion tons.
A giant star runs out of fuel. Its core collapses in seconds — gravity crushes it until almost everything left is neutrons.
The result: 1.4 times the mass of our Sun, packed into a sphere about 20 kilometers wide.
One sugar cube of that material weighs about a billion tons — 170 Great Pyramids of Giza balanced on your fingertips.
Drop a piece here and it wouldn't rest on the floor. It would punch straight through the crust.
We only found these in 1967, when a telescope caught a signal flashing every 1.3 seconds. They called it LGM — Little Green Men.
The nearest known neutron star is 400 light-years away. Even Voyager would need seven million years to deliver that sugar cube. Better left where they are.
